header.tolerance: within 5% is at market; more than 15% is well above or well below
header.competitor_set_note: Brewline Supply and Kettlemere Home were named by the user; Burrvale Goods was added from Merchant Center's top merchants (page overlap 37%). marketplace.example (overlap 55%) is a marketplace with many sellers, so the Amazon seller export stands in for marketplace prices; bigbox-home.example overlaps on 12% of pages and was left out.

top_findings.finding: Shipping, not the item price, makes the brewers look expensive: 4 of 4 brewers pay $6.95 shipping because your free-shipping threshold is $75, while Kettlemere Home starts at $49, Brewline Supply at $50 and Burrvale Goods ships every order at no charge. On item price alone the brewers are only 1.4% to 7.7% above the median item price of the rival shops (the Amazon export is a delivered price, so it is left out here); on landed price they are 9.2% to 14.6% above.
top_findings.action: Cut the brewers under the beat rule within the 10% limit, and test a lower free-shipping threshold before cutting further.

top_findings.finding: Kettles are priced over the market: 2 of 3 are well above (22.3%, 24.2%) and one is above (7.0%) the median landed price of in-stock rivals.
top_findings.action: Cut 3 kettles under the match rule; the two well-above ones stop at the 10% limit and need another run.

top_findings.finding: The conical burr grinder sits 11.6% under the market even though Brewline Supply's grinders are on a sale.
top_findings.action: Raise it under the match rule, by the 10% limit this run.

group_rules.rule: Grinders: match the median landed price of in-stock rivals, never below each product's floor or above list price, moving at most 10% per weekly run.
Kettles: match the median landed price of in-stock rivals, never below each product's floor or above list price, moving at most 10% per weekly run.
Brewers: price 2% under the lowest in-stock rival landed price, never below each product's floor or above list price, moving at most 10% per weekly run.
Filters and accessories: match the median landed price of in-stock rivals, never below each product's floor or above list price, moving at most 10% per weekly run.
Coffee (own brand): hold the price; report the gap only.
